About Newpage Solutions

Your Mission

We are hiring a Fullstack Developer who knows the Gemini platform from the inside how Gemini Enterprise is administered, how agents, data connectors, extensions and Gems are built, registered, scoped and distributed, and how access and permissions actually flow through them.

You will be embedded with a large enterprise client as part of a small engineering pod, alongside engineers who own other enterprise AI platforms. You will own the path by which new data connectors, agents and skills reach users: from intake through access group creation, identity provider synchronisation, connector registration, per-tool permission scoping, testing, documentation and closure with the requester. You will review third-party components for security and quality before release, and replace manual console work with automated, repeatable pipelines.

This is not an administration role. Most of your time goes into building: the backend services, data mappings and integrations that wire the platform into the client's systems, and the internal tooling that gives platform owners visibility and control over how AI capabilities are being used. You should be as strong in the backend APIs, identity, data, infrastructure as code as you are in the UI.

You won't wait for a refined backlog or a separate platform team. You will take a vague request, work out what is actually needed, build it, and stand it up in production yourself. This is a builder role for engineers who combine solid fullstack fundamentals with a deep, practical understanding of the Gemini platform and its extension model.

What You'll Do

Build & Integrate


Design and build the backend services, APIs and data mappings that connect Gemini to enterprise systems identity, data sources, ticketing and the connectors in between.
Build internal tooling and admin interfaces (React / Next.js over Python or TypeScript backends) that give platform owners visibility into usage and control over which capabilities are available to whom.
Build or integrate agents and extensions for the client's own use cases Agent Designer, ADK, Gemini CLI extensions, or LLM-powered services and agents on whichever orchestration framework fits (LangGraph, Google ADK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents SDK or similar), integrating models through APIs, tool calling / MCP and structured outputs and register them in Gemini Enterprise so the right people can use them.
Take a vague request from a business or platform owner, work out what is actually needed, ship a working version quickly, and harden what survives contact with real users.


Own Connector & Agent Requests End to End


Own data connector, agent and skill requests for the enterprise Gemini platform from intake through to closure with the requester.
Create access groups and manage identity provider synchronisation (SSO / SCIM with Okta, Entra ID or Google Cloud Identity) so access follows existing team and group structures.
Register connectors and data stores and apply per-tool permission scoping, granting only the access each capability needs.
Test each connector and agent before release, document what it does and how to use it, and close the loop with the requester.


Configure, Distribute & Review Platform Capabilities


Configure and distribute agents, skills, extensions and Gems to the right audience enterprise-wide, group-scoped or on request with a clear understanding of the scoping controls and what each one actually gates.
Conduct security and quality reviews of third-party and externally authored agents, extensions and connectors before release: dependencies, bundled scripts, and exposure to prompt injection or data exfiltration.
Define remediation or approval decisions and document them so the standard is repeatable.


Automate Provisioning


Automate setup, registration and provisioning through CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code (Terraform) in place of manual console configuration.
Build parameterised deployments across development, staging and production environments.
Turn recurring manual requests into reusable, version-controlled automation.


What You Bring


5+ years building production fullstack applications in Python and TypeScript APIs, integrations and modern web frameworks (FastAPI, Node / Fastify, React / Next.js). You are backend-strong: data mappings, integration plumbing and wiring systems together is where you spend most of your time, not just the UI.
Deep, hands-on knowledge of the Gemini platform: Gemini Enterprise administration (data connectors and data stores, agent registration, end-user feature controls, IdP-synced groups and access) and the Gemini API, plus Gemini for Google Workspace (Gems and admin controls) where it is in use. Hands-on experience with Gemini function calling / tool use and MCP servers, including tool permissions and capability scoping.
Hands-on experience building agents or LLM integrations with at least one orchestration framework (LangGraph, Google ADK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, OpenAI Agents SDK or similar), and comfortable switching the team's framework is not fixed.
Security-minded reviewing of code and AI components: dependency analysis, script review, and a practical understanding of prompt injection and data exfiltration risks.
CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Cloud Build or similar) and infrastructure as code with Terraform across AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, including parameterised multi-environment deployments.
Structured, disciplined use of AI-assisted development (Gemini CLI, Claude Code or similar) with review, not on autopilot.
Clear written communication, and the confidence to reframe a vague request into something concrete rather than wait for someone else to define it.
Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science or a related technical discipline.


Bonus Skills / Experience


Working knowledge of a second enterprise AI platform Claude (Claude Enterprise, Claude Code), Microsoft Copilot Studio, AWS Bedrock or Azure AI Foundry. A strong plus: you will be expected to provide cover across platforms.
Background in AppSec, supply-chain security or security review processes.
Experience in pharma, life sciences or other regulated industries.

A recent public trail of built things GitHub, side projects, OSS contributions, or writing about building with AI.

A people-first culture supportive peers, open communication, and a strong sense of belonging.
Smart, purposeful collaboration work with talented colleagues to create technologies that solve meaningful business challenges.
Balance that lasts we respect your time and support a healthy integration of work and life.
Room to grow opportunities for learning, leadership, and career development, shaped around you.
Meaningful rewards competitive compensation that recognises both contribution and potential.

We are an early-stage company building applied AI products for complex professional workflows, including healthcare and legal.

The Role

We are looking for a hands-on engineering leader who can own multiple AI products end-to-end—not just an AI component, backend service, or prototype.

You will take products from requirements and architecture through implementation, integration, testing, deployment, and ongoing operation. The work spans AI-powered applications, voice and document workflows, knowledge systems, and the shared infrastructure supporting them.

You will work directly with the founder, who leads product direction, priorities, and customer requirements. You will own engineering execution and technical decisions, enabling the founder to focus on product rather than daily code reviews, debugging, and integration management.

This is a player-coach role: you will write production code, lead a small engineering team, and remain accountable for whether the complete product actually works.

End-to-end product delivery. Turn product requirements into working applications across the frontend, backend, AI layer, data systems, and infrastructure. Own the complete user journey—not merely whether individual components run.
Architecture and technical decisions. Choose appropriate technologies, define clear interfaces, and make practical build-versus-buy decisions. Build reusable capabilities across products without creating unnecessary abstraction or complexity.

CAI Business Units and the Markets We Serve




CAI Software is organized into three business units: Graphic Communications, Process Manufacturing, and Discrete Manufacturing - aligned to the industries we serve. This structure keeps our teams close to customer needs while operating with the scale and support of a global software company.




This role is part of our Discrete Manufacturing business unit, which delivers software solutions for manufacturers that produce components and assemblies that become part of larger products. Serving small through enterprise manufacturers in industries such as aerospace, automotive, industrial equipment, and engineered products, Discrete Manufacturing focuses on modern execution—connecting planning, production, traceability, and automation to help manufacturers run more resilient, efficient, and predictable operations. 







CAI India 

CAI India is a strategic investment in the company’s future. Our Bangalore Center of Excellence is a place of ownership, expertise, and accountability. Teams in India work on global products end to end, contribute to key decisions, and influence how CAI evolves as a business. About the Role

Act as a technical architect for the legacy-to-modern transformation of the EDI Products platform — proposing target-state architecture, evaluating trade-offs, and documenting decisions.
Design and build full stack features end-to-end: Angular/TypeScript front end, .NET-based middleware (HarmonyCore), and the underlying data layer (ISAM/SQL-style access).

Use AI-assisted development tools as a core part of the daily workflow — for implementation, refactoring, test generation, and code review — and help raise the bar for AI-led development practices across the team.
Apply working knowledge of EDI concepts (trading-partner transactions, ASNs, mapping/translation, X12 standards) to ensure modernization work preserves business-critical behavior.
Break down architecture and epics into well-scoped stories in Azure DevOps (ADO), and manage code through ADO-Git (branching, pull requests, code review).
Collaborate with the Engineering Manager and Product Managers/Product Owners in Aha! to align technical planning with roadmap priorities.
Keep architecture decisions, designs, and technical documentation current in Confluence for the team and cross-functional stakeholders.
Mentor other engineers on full stack development practices, code quality, and modernization patterns.
Identify technical risk and legacy-system pitfalls early, and propose pragmatic mitigation paths.




AI-Led Development




This role is expected to model AI-led development for the team:

Use AI coding assistants fluently for implementation, debugging, refactoring, and test coverage across the stack.
Apply sound judgment about when and how to use AI-generated code responsibly, especially around legacy business logic.
Contribute to team norms/guardrails for secure, effective AI tool usage.




Tools & Platforms




Azure DevOps (ADO) and ADO-Git
Aha! (roadmap and planning alignment)
Confluence (architecture and engineering documentation)
AI-assisted development tooling as adopted by the organization




Required Qualifications




Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field from a Tier-1 or Tier-2 institution (e.g., IITs, NITs, IIITs, or equivalent top-ranked engineering colleges) strongly preferred.
5+ years of professional full stack development experience, with demonstrated ability to work across front end, middleware, and data layers.
Strong front-end skills in Angular (or equivalent modern framework) and TypeScript/JavaScript.
Strong back-end skills in .NET / C#, with experience designing and building APIs and middleware services.
Solid understanding of relational and/or legacy data access patterns (SQL; exposure to ISAM or similar older data stores is a plus).
Experience or working knowledge of EDI (electronic data interchange) concepts — X12 standards, trading-partner transactions, ASNs, or mapping/translation tools.
Demonstrated experience acting in an architect-level capacity: system design, technology trade-off analysis, and technical documentation.
Hands-on, daily experience using AI-assisted development tools in a professional setting.
Experience working in Azure DevOps (ADO/ADO-Git) for planning and source control.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain architectural decisions to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.




Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Synergy DBL, ExtJS, or other legacy enterprise stacks.
Experience with Aha! for roadmap planning and Confluence for architecture documentation.
Background in automotive, manufacturing, or B2B integration software domains.




What Success Looks Like




A clear, well-documented target architecture for modernizing the EDI Products platform, with team buy-in.
Tangible modernization progress shipped incrementally, without disrupting existing customer-facing functionality.
Visible, effective use of AI-led development that measurably improves delivery speed and code quality.
Strong technical documentation in Confluence and clean, well-managed work in ADO/ADO-Git.
